newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia goes to the Net after new disease kills 15.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia goes to the Net after new disease kills 15.

text.p: An outbreak of a new strain of an airborne disease has killed at least 15 children in Malaysia's Borneo state of Sarawak and health officials have turned to the Internet for help.

At least 15 other children, suspected to be suffering from a new strain of Coxsackie B, are in an isolation ward in Sibu, a timber town on the coast of Sarawak, an official at Sibu hospital told Reuters on Wednesday.

A team of senior medical officers from Kuala Lumpur was in Sibu on Wednesday to assess the extent of the outbreak which first hit on April 14, killing children in Sibu, the state capital of Kuching, and in the town of Sarikei.
The Sarawak Health Department has put out a notice on the Internet, describing the disease and asking for help.
The symptoms include a fever lasting two or three days, an attack on the nervous system manifested as fits and paralysis of one side of the upper limbs, and finally, heart failure.

"As we have yet to come to a conclusive diagnosis of this condition, we would be very grateful if anyone could provide some information or suggestion as to what organism we are dealing with," said the page (http://www.jaring.my/jkns/outbreak/virus1.htm).
"This is essential for control purposes," it added.

The health department's notice said six of the cases came from within the same district, but the rest were from different localities. The victims were aged between five months and 3-1/2 years. They all died of heart failure.
"All cases were very ill when admitted to hospital and died within 24 hours of admission," the notice said.

The Malaysian health ministry said it has also sought help from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta. The World Health Organisation (WHO) said it was working with Malaysian authorities in researching the disease.
"This is a very new disease. We want to get more information," a spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday.

Health officials said the disease was spread through eating infected food, or from insects that have come in contact with the infected food. Hospital staff treating the children in the isolation ward are wearing masks and caps and change their hospital uniforms afterward due to the lethal nature of the airborne disease, officials in Sibu said. Health Minister Chua Jui Meng said earlier this week the outbreak was puzzling to officials because Coxsackie strains did not usually cause heart failure.
